thread.title: Tech Today: Trump vs Amazon, Facebook Bounces Back, Waymo Motors On

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Trump vs Amazon, Facebook Bounces Back, Waymo Motors On
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech:
The Fang gang is trading mixed this morning, with bad rumors weighing down Amazon.com ( AMZN ) but Facebook ( FB ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) getting a reprieve after yesterday’s intense tech sell-off .
Trump obsessed with Amazon
U.S. President Donald Trump has a continuing dislike for Amazon , writes Jonathan Swan of Axios , citing five unnamed sources who claim the president is “obsessed” with the company.
Trump continues to make claims to “people” about Amazon getting away with special treatment on taxes , something he brought up repeatedly on the campaign trail in 2016.
A source tells Swan, "He’s wondered aloud if there may be any way to go after Amazon with antitrust or competition law.” Another source says Trump “would love to clip CEO Jeff Bezos’s wings, but he doesn’t have a plan to make that happen.”
Amazon stock is down $59.22, or almost 4%, at $1,437.83.
Facebook’s data risk
Facebook is actually in the green this morning, up $2.57, or 1.6%, at $154.79, after it unveiled its new privacy controls in a longish description posted in its newsroom Web site. The company’s chief privacy officer , Erin Egan , describes how Facebook has tried to make it easier for people to control their privacy.
For instance, the settings menu for privacy has been condensed to a single screen, down from 20 separate screens, and there is now a shortcut menu for privacy controls.
Morgan Stanley ’s Brian Nowak , reviewing the changes, writes that the changes are “important steps” on Facebook’s part, but he observes there is "a negative feedback risk that users will choose to materially reduce FB’s access to their data."
"As such, it will be important to monitor and survey user reactions and behaviors once these tools are rolled out,” writes Nowak.
In other Facebook news, Jon Swartz related last night how CEO and founder Mark Zuckerberg is going to testify before U.S. lawmakers.
Waymo keeps on truckin'
Alphabet suddenly looks brilliant by comparison to other techs given that its Waymo self-driving car effort is not backing down.
While Nvidia ( NVDA ), for example, yesterday said it would suspend self-driving car tests on the road , Waymo was holding a media event in New York to discuss a partnership with Jaguar to add more Jags to the Waymo fleet.
My colleague Emily Bary at MarketWatch has the run-down on that .
Aegis Capital ’s Victor Anthony , who has a Buy rating on Google stock, and a $1,350 price target, reviews the Waymo-Jag partnership, and concludes that "Waymo is plowing ahead in the midst of challenges by others."
Writes Anthony, "The recent challenges faced by competitors will only further Waymo's lead in this evolving and disruptive industry."
Shares of Alphabet are up $15.22, or 1.5%, at $1,022.16.
More trouble in iPhone-land
Another day, another cut in estimates for Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone — and from multiple different parties.
Goldman Sachs ’s Rod Hall , who has a Neutral rating on the stock, lowered his numbers for both the March quarter and the June quarter, writing that "early CQ1 demand indications suggest even lower actual numbers than consensus is modeling.”
Demand is “weak” for iPhone and getting weaker, writes Hall, something that will leave Apple with 1 million units in inventory in June, he believes, “which is atypical."
Also cutting is Jun Zhang of Rosenblatt , who reduces his production estimates for Apple for the June-ending quarter. Zhang cites Samsung Electronics (005930KS) having cut its production of the recently released “Galaxy S9,” writing "we continue to believe the high-end smartphone market is not recovering ."
Apple shares are down 77 cents, or half a percent, at $167.57.
